paper_metadata.title: Alternative pipeline for option pricing using quantum computers

summary: The paper proposes a gate-based quantum option-pricing pipeline combining direct encoding with modified real quantum amplitude estimation (mRQAE). It reports emulator-based experiments on 5-qubit Black-Scholes discretizations for vanilla/digital options and a 10-qubit cliquet setup, with the key result that naive square-root encoding fails on negative payoffs while the direct-encoding+mRQAE pipeline recovers the sign and is competitive with mIQAE. The claimed asymptotic gain is the standard amplitude-estimation improvement from O(1/ε^2) to O(1/ε), but no practical hardware advantage is demonstrated.

experiments.description: Quantum accelerated Monte Carlo option-pricing experiments using square-root encoding and modified iterative quantum amplitude estimation (mIQAE) on positive-payoff vanilla/digital options and a cliquet option, evaluated on a quantum emulator.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Accelerated Monte Carlo (QAMC) with square-root encoding and mIQAE
algorithm.convergence_criteria: target precision ϵ and confidence 1-γ in mIQAE

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Black-Scholes path distribution encoded into amplitudes; square-root payoff encoding used to place sqrt(F) into the amplitude of an ancilla qubit
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate discounted expected payoff V_t = e^{-r(T-t)} E_Q[V_T|F_t] for vanilla call, digital call, vanilla put, digital put, linear payoff, and cliquet options

problem_instance.description: Derivative pricing under Black-Scholes model for several payoff types, including a path-dependent cliquet option

dataset_specification.description: Single-asset Black-Scholes with discretized terminal-price distribution; cliquet uses one reset date and maturity at two years

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Discretize standard normal / Black-Scholes distribution into 32 points between 0.01 and 5.0; for cliquet, 1024 paths from 32 reset-date points and 32 maturity points
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Absolute error versus discretized expectation plotted against number of oracle calls; medians and 25/75 percentiles reported

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Black-Scholes distribution discretization; exact simulation of terminal asset price under Black-Scholes
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Convert estimated probability to expected payoff and compare with discretized expectation

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: absolute error decreases with oracle calls; medians and interquartile range shown

speedup_claims.conditions: amplitude estimation with oracle calls scaling as O(1/epsilon) versus Monte Carlo O(1/epsilon^2)
speedup_claims.caveats: Empirical comparison is on a quantum emulator; no physical QPU results.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(1/ϵ) oracle calls for amplitude estimation; QAMC quadratic improvement over Monte Carlo

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; experiments use a 5-qubit discretization for single-step Black-Scholes and 10 qubits for the cliquet example.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: The paper reports O(1/ε) oracle calls for amplitude estimation versus O(1/ε^2) for Monte Carlo, but only on a quantum emulator and with small discretized instances.

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because experiments were performed on CESGA infrastructure using QLM/myQLM emulator software, not a physical QPU.
Circuit depth not explicitly reported; only oracle-call scaling and algorithmic depth discussion are given.
Authors claim the pipeline retains speedups relative to standard QAMC, but the evidence is emulator-based and not a practical advantage demonstration.
